<entry id="C00144">
<head-word>גַּבְשׁוּשִׁית</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (גבש) 
<italic>heap of stones, pile, mound</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. 73
<sup>b</sup>. Ib. 152
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Koh. XII, 5 מגבוה ייראו) שאפי' ג' קטנה וכ' even a small mound appears to him (the aged man) like the highest mountains. Y. Erub. II, 20
<sup>a</sup>, opp. חָרִיץ.—
<plural-form>Pl. גַּבְשׁוּשִׁיֹּות</plural-form>. Y. Sot. VII, 21
<sup>c</sup> שתי ג' וכ' (not … שית) they put up two mounds and named them Mount Gerizim &c.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="C00153">
<head-word>גַּד, </head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<head-word>גָּדָד</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (גדד, cmp. חד) [
<italic>cutting</italic>,] 
<italic>bitter, acrid</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ex. R. s. 5 (ref. to Num. XI, 7) מר וגד bitter and acrid. Targ. B’shall., ed. Bub. 21 גד ולענה (read כלענה; Yalk. Ex. 258 מר כלע').—
<plural-form>Pl. גַּדִּים, גַּדִּין, גְּדָדִין</plural-form>. Gen. R. s. 71 (play on 
<italic>Gaddi</italic>, Num. XIII, 1</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition />
<notes> [read:] גְּדָדִין ומררין acrid and bitter (people); Yalk. Gen. 126 כגידין מררין, v. 
<xref rid="unknown">גִּידָּא II</xref>; Yalk. Ezra 1067 בר גדי (corr. acc.). [גדין, Targ. Y. Num. XXII, 7 Ar. s. v. גדין, read אִגְּרִין.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="C00154">
<head-word>גַּד, </head-word>
<hw-number>II</hw-number>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="K00104"> cmp. כַּד II)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>a rounded-off seed grain, coriander</italic>, (in Talm. a. Midr.) 
<italic>linseed</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yoma 75
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Ex. XVI, 7) עגול כגִידָּא וכ' the manna resembled a grain by its rounded shape, and a pearl by its white color; even so it has been taught גד שדומה לזרע וכ' the word 
<italic>gad</italic> (grain) is used, because the manna resembled linseed; Yalk. Ex. 261; Num. 734. Mekh. B’shall., Vayassa, 5 (ref. to Ex. l. c.) איני יודע של מי דומה I do not know to which the comparison refers (to shape or to color); … דומה לזרע וכ' it resembles (in form) linseed: but you might think &c., ת"ל לבן therefore ‘white’ is added.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="C00155">
<head-word>גָּד, </head-word>
<head-word>גַּד, </head-word>
<hw-number>III</hw-number>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="C00153"> גדד</xref>,
<xref rid="A00083"> cmp. גזר)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>decree, fate</italic>, esp. 
<italic>Gad</italic> (
<italic>Fortune</italic>), a god worshipped by the Babylonians and the Jewish exiles.</definition>
<notes> Snh. 63
<sup>b</sup> ג' נמי מיכתב כתיב Gad is also one of the names of idols mentioned in the Bible. 
<pgbrk id="pg210" />Sabb. 67
<sup>b</sup> ג' אינו אלא לשון ע"א Gad is nothing else than a designation of an idol, v. next w.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> גַּד יָוָן
<pos> pr. n.</pos>
<italic>Gad Yavan</italic> (
<italic>Greek Fortune</italic>) near Jerusalem.</definition>
<notes> Zab. I, 5 כְּמִן ג' י' לשילוה as long as it takes from G. Y. to Siloah; Tosef. ib. I, 10 כְּמִגַּדְיָוָן לשילה; Snh. 63
<sup>b</sup> כְּמִיגַּדְיָוָן לשילה (corr. acc.)—[
<italic>Gad Yavan</italic> is prob. the name of a pool connected with the Siloah, perh. 
<italic>Fount of the Virgin</italic>, v. Sm. Bible Dict. s. v. Siloam.] [Toh. VI, 6; Erub. 22
<sup>b</sup> בית גד גד, v. גִּלְגּוּל.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="C00156">
<head-word>גָּד, </head-word>
<head-word>גַּדָּא</head-word>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>
<language-reference>same</language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, 
<italic>luck; genius, godhead</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. O. Gen. XXX, 11 גָּד; Y. II גַּדָּא (not גֵּרָא). Targ. Esth. VIII, 15 גַּדָּא (not גָּדָא).—Gen. R. s. 71 ג' דביתא the good genius of the house. Sabb. 67
<sup>b</sup> גד גַּרִּי וסינוק לא (Ms. M. צינוק), a charm formula supposed to mean, 
<italic>Be lucky, my luck, and tire not</italic> (prob. 
<italic>Grow, my luck</italic> &c., v. נְגַד). Ḥull. 40
<sup>a</sup> לג' דהר to the godhead of the mountain. Ned. 56
<sup>a</sup> (explain. דרגש) ערסא דג' the bed reserved for the domestic genius (bed of state). Y. Ab. Zar. I, 39
<sup>d</sup> top לגַרֵּיה וכ', v. ארקליס. Gen. R. s. 65 ג' דע"ז דאת קאים [ביה] by the idolatrous godhead by whom thou standest, i.e. to whom thou referrest in saying, ‘Let my father rise’ (Gen. XXVII, 31). Y. Sabb. XVI, end, 15
<sup>d</sup>; Y. Yoma VIII, 45
<sup>b</sup>; Y. Ned. IV, 38
<sup>d</sup> בגַדָּךְ מדלי (not בגרך) doest thou rely upon thy good luck? Koh. R. to VII, 26 מה ביש ג' וכ' how bad is this woman’s (my) luck!; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. גַּדַּיָּיא, גַּדַּיָּא</plural-form>. Y. Ab. Zar. III, 43
<sup>a</sup> bot. ג' קורין אותה גליא a place called 
<italic>Gaddaya</italic> is cacophemistically named 
<italic>Gallaya</italic> (dung-hills); Tosef. ib. VI (VII), 4 גדגיא ed. Zuck. (ed. גריא, corr. acc.).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="C00166">
<head-word>גָּדַד, </head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="C00537"> cmp. גזז</xref>,
<xref rid="A00083"> קצץ)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to cut, cut off.</italic></definition>
<notes> Par. II, 2; Bekh. 44
<sup>a</sup> יָגוֹד let him lop off (the black tops of the horns or hoofs).—[V. גָּדַר.]—Trnsf. (cmp. קצץ) 
<italic>to fix the price</italic>. B. Bath. 13
<sup>a</sup> גּוֹד או אָגוֹד either fix you a price for my share, or I shall do so (and buy your share); דינא דגוד או אגוד the right of settling by 
<italic>god o agod</italic>. Ib. אגוד איכא גוד ליכא the offer to buy is applicable in this case (the half-freed slave can offer to buy his other half), but the offer to sell cannot be made (since there is no price for a free man).—
<italic>Part. pass</italic>. גָּדוּד 
<italic>stripped</italic> (of branches); trnsf. 
<italic>empty-handed</italic>. Gen. R. s. 68, beg. ג' שלחו (Yalk. ib. 117 גדודי) Isaac sent Jacob away without anything valuable.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>גִּדֵּד</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to cut off, level</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 71 (play on בא גד, Gen. XXX, 1</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition />
<notes> בא מי שעתיד לגַדֵּד וכ' he has come who is destined to level the fastnesses of the nations (idolatry). Tanḥ. Ki Thissa 13 (play on מגדל גד, Josh. XV, 37) from there the Lord יוצא ומְגַדֵּד וכ' will proceed and level &c.; Ex. R. s. 40 ומגיד (corr. acc.).</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִגְדַּד</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be cut off</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Keth. 51
<sup>a</sup> כל העומד לִיגָּדֵד כְּגָדוּד דמי Ar. (ed. ליגזז, v. גָּזַז).</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpol.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְגּוֹדֵד</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to make incisions in one’s own body</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yeb. 13
<sup>b</sup>, v. גּוּד. Tanḥ. Sh’laḥ. 15; Num. R. s. 17 קבר מת לא תִתְגּוֹדְדוּ when one buried a dead, the law says, Ye shall not &c. (Deut. XIV, 1). V. גְּדִידָה.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>*.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>גֹּדֵד</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> same.</definition>
<notes> Yeb. l. c. א"כ לימא קרא לא תְּגוֹדְדוּ if it were so (that Deut. XIV, 1 meant only to forbid incisions in the body) it ought to read 
<italic>lo t’god’du</italic>, ye shall make no incisions.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>

<italic>to rear, train.</italic></definition>

<pgbrk id="pg213" />they let their hair grow (in mourning). Erub. 100
<sup>b</sup> מְגַדָּלֶת שער she lets her hair grow (does not cut it); a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to raise to dignity, make famous; to praise</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Hor. 9
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Lev. XXI, 10) whence do we know אם אין לו שחייבין לגַדְּלוֹ when he (the Highpriest) is poor, that they (the brethren) are bound to raise him (make him independent)? Ib. גַּדְּלֵהוּ משל אחיו raise him by a collection from his brethren (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l.). Esth. R. to III, 1 למה גִדְּלוֹ for what purpose did (the Lord) raise him? Yalk. Esth. 1053 עד היכן גִּידְּלוֹ וכ' how high did he raise him? Fifty cubits (to the gallows); a. fr.—Y. Meg. III, end, 74
<sup>c</sup> (ref. to הגדול, Neh. VIII, 6) במה גִידְּלֹו wherewith did he magnify the Lord (describe His greatness)?; Yoma 69
<sup>b</sup> ג' בשם וכ' he praised the Lord by pronouncing the tetragrammaton; Y. Ber. VII, 11
<sup>c</sup> גודלו (corr. acc.)—Part. pass. מְגוּדָּל 
<italic>well grown</italic>. Ber. 11
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.—Kidd. 49
<sup>a</sup>, 
<sup>b</sup>, v. גַּדֶּלֶת.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>

<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>

<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, 
<italic>Nithpa</italic>.</definition>
<notes> נִתְגַּדֵּל </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be raised</italic> to dignity.</definition>
<notes> Esth. R. to III, 1 יִתְגַּדֵּל ואח"כ יתלה let him first become great and then be hanged. Gen. R. s. 99, end (play on פֹּרָת, Gen. XLIX, 2</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition> ע"י פָּרוֹת נ' by means of cows (Pharaoh’s dream) was he raised to power; a. fr.— 
<italic>to be magnified</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Ber. IX, 14
<sup>a</sup> top; Y. Taan. I, 64
<sup>b</sup> top יִתְגַּדֵּל וכ' may Thy Name be glorified, sanctified &c.; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to glorify one’s self, to boast, parade</italic>.</definition>

<sup>a</sup>; Ab. IV, 5 אל תעשם עטרה להִתְגַּדֵּל בהם make them (the words of the Law) not a crown to parade therewith.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—4)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to grow, prosper, be nursed</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tanḥ. V’zoth 1; Pesik. ib. p. 199
<sup>a</sup> הרי … מִתְגַּדֵּל עמו the poison-bearing tree will be nursed along with it (the health-giving tree). Tanḥ. B’resh. 7 נִתְגַּדַּלְתָּ וחטאת thou didst grow older and didst sin, opp. תינוק היית; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

Snh. VII, 25

<sup>b</sup> bot. דלת גודרת וכ'; Tosef. ib. XI (VII), 18 גוררת ed. Zuck., Var. גוד', v. גָּרַר.]—[Y. Sabb. XV, 15

<notes> Targ. Ex. XIV, 22; a. fr.—Y. Peah VIII, 20
<sup>d</sup> bot. מן גּוֹא לפסא out of the pot. Ḥull. 41
<sup>a</sup> אית ליה שותפות בגַוָּהּ he owns a share in it. Ib. 48

<sup>b</sup> bot. גו שמשא in the sun (in sunlight); a. v. fr.—מן גו, מִגּוֹ, מִיגּוֹ 
<italic>because, in consequence of</italic>. Y. Taan. II, 65
<sup>b</sup>, v. בּוּךְ. Y. Ber. I, 3
<sup>b</sup> top מן גו דאינון ציבחר because they are brief.—B. Mets. 39
<sup>b</sup> מיגו דמוקמינן וכ' since we have to appoint a guardian for &c. Ib. 5
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. מ' דחשיד אממונא וכ' since he is suspected of wrong-doing in money matters, he is also suspected of swearing falsely; a. fr.—Hence מִיגּוֹ, מִגּוֹ

<sup>b</sup>, and מֵאַחַר, v. אַחַר) 
<italic>a legal rule according to which a deponent’s statement is accepted as true on the ground that, if he had intended to tell a lie, he might have invented one more advantageous to his case</italic> (cmp. B. Bath. 31
<sup>a</sup> מה לו לשקר אי בעי וכ' why should he lie? If he wanted to lie, he might have said &c.). Keth. 16
<sup>a</sup> התם מאי מ' איכא what 
<italic>miggo</italic> is there in that case, i.e. what choice did she have in inventing a statement, if she intended to tell a lie? Ib. מכדי האי מ' והאי מ' וכ' since in this case there is the legal presumption of a 
<italic>miggo</italic>, and so is in the other, what is the difference between the one 
<italic>miggo</italic> and the other?; a. fr.—2) (cmp. אַגַּב) 
<italic>an action declared valid because one part of it was indisputably legitimate</italic>, or 
<italic>because the legal status required for its legitimacy might easily have been obtained</italic>. B. Mets. 9
<sup>b</sup> מ' דאי בעי מפקר וכ' since, if he wanted, he might have declared his possession public property, in which case he would have obtained the legal status of poverty entitling him to the corner of the field (פֵּאָה), and since (if he had resigned his property) he would have been entitled to take possession of the corner for himself, he has a right also to take possession of it in behalf of his neighbor. Ib. תרי מ' לא אמרינן two 
<italic>miggos</italic> cannot be accepted, i.e. two conditions required to make an action legitimate cannot be dispensed with. Ib. 8
<sup>a</sup>. Ned. 88
<sup>b</sup>; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
